content: {"summary":"On 22 Mar 2025 the payments‑api latency rose and PAYAPI‑E1042 errors appeared while clients waited in PgBouncer despite idle server connections. The logs show PgBouncer’s process using 96 % of a single CPU core, and the runbook notes that PgBouncer is a single‑process using one core and that 100 % CPU while `sv_idle`>0 indicates the bouncer itself is the bottleneck. The service status also marks payments‑pgbouncer as degraded, confirming the CPU‑related issue.","likely_cause":"PgBouncer CPU saturation (near‑full use of its single core) causing it to become the bottleneck and queue client connections, leading to PAYAPI‑E1042 and rising latency.","confidence":"medium","claims":[{"text":"PgBouncer CPU was at 96 % of one core during the incident","evidence_ids":["log:1129"],"quote":"pgbouncer process cpu at 96% of one core"},{"text":"PgBouncer runs as a single process using one core, so high usage indicates saturation","evidence_ids":["RB-011#3"],"quote":"PgBouncer is a single process using one core"},{"text":"When PgBouncer is pinned at ~100 % CPU while server connections are idle, it is the bottleneck","evidence_ids":["RB-011#4"],"quote":"the bouncer is the bottleneck"},{"text":"The payments‑pgbouncer service was reported degraded at the time","evidence_ids":["status:payments-pgbouncer"],"quote":"payments-pgbouncer: degraded (owner team-payments; depends on payments-db)"}],"next_checks":["Monitor PgBouncer CPU usage continuously","Check `sv_idle` metrics to confirm idle server connections while CPU is high","Verify that PgBouncer reloads reduce CPU load","Consider scaling PgBouncer or adjusting pool settings if CPU remains saturated"]}
